justification: Assessment reported INVALID and localized the failure to Step 2, lines 0039-0040, the claim P - C = {x : Ax <= b} justified by A(x - c) = Ax - Ac <= b - 0 = b. That is exactly the ground-truth flaw ('if x in P and c in C then x - c in P'). The witness differs in sign convention but is independently valid: with A = [1], b = 0, P = (-inf, 0], C = {d : d <= 0}; x = 0 in P, c = -5 in C, x - c = 5 and A(x - c) = 5 > 0 = b, so x - c is not in P. Same sign-slip defect, different-but-correct counterexample; the extra P - C = R and X + C = (-inf, r] computations also check out.
